dial.summary: Global M2 at $102.7T and Fed balance sheet at $6.75T maintain the macro liquidity floor; with the FOMC two-day meeting beginning tomorrow (July 28), BTC.D at 56.3%, TOTAL steady at $2.28T, and perp funding rates easing to +0.004%/8h, the accumulation setup holds—a dovish Warsh hold on July 29 remains the key catalyst needed to break DXY (currently 101.18 and dipping) below 100 and bring real yields toward the 2% neutral threshold.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: 4-bank aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) at approximately $102.7T per MacroMicro series (May 2026 vintage, confirmed at $102,653B per latest update); US M2 continues to expand at multi-year high growth rates; China M2 ~$50T at ~9% YoY; EU M2 ~$19.4T; Japan ~$9T; 4-week trend up: global M2 uptrend sustained across all major components with YoY growth positive and accelerating; status supportive (4-week uptrend confirmed; contracting-YoY headwind condition not met).

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: June 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 53.3% (released July 1)—sixth consecutive expansion month, down from May's 54.0%; July 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI releases Monday August 3, 2026 at 10:00 AM ET; sub-indicators from June: new orders 56.0%, production 52.2%, employment 49.7% (contracting), prices paid 73.0% (-9.1pp—largest single-month drop since July 2022); 4-week trend down (May 54.0% → June 53.3%); status neutral (above 50 but falling—supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 and falling).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY spot at 101.18 on July 27, 2026, down 0.28% from the prior close of 101.47; July 24 close confirmed at 101.46; 4-week trend flat: DXY moved from ~101.43 (June 25 close) to 101.18 (July 27)—change of -0.25%, within the <0.5% relative flat threshold; DXY has traded in a 101.1–101.5 range through late July; status headwind (ICE DXY above the 100 threshold; supportive threshold is below 97.5); July 28–29 FOMC dovish guidance is the primary near-term catalyst for a sustained break below 100.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: 10-year TIPS real yield (DFII10) at 2.37% as of July 24, 2026 (MacroRadar/FRED); up ~4.9% over the past 12 months; 4-week trend up: DFII10 rose approximately +0.19pp from ~2.18% on June 25 to 2.37% on July 24—well above the 5bp flat threshold; status headwind (above 2% and rising on 4-week basis); July 30 Q2 GDP advance and June PCE are the next disinflation tests; a dovish FOMC and soft PCE could begin compressing real yields toward the 2.00% neutral threshold.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: 10-year Treasury at 4.69%, 2-year at 4.34% (July 24 close, latest confirmed); spread: 4.69% − 4.34% = +0.35%; updated from prior run's +0.34% as 10Y edged up 2bps; 4-week trend flat: spread was approximately +0.39–0.40% on June 25, now +0.35%—narrowing of ~5bps, near the flat boundary; status neutral (positive spread well clear of the −50bps deep-inversion headwind threshold; not steepening on 30-day basis; FOMC dovish guidance is primary near-term steepening catalyst).

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL confirmed at $6.75T for week ending July 22, 2026 (Convex/FRED H.4.1, released July 24); next H.4.1 release July 30, 2026 (week ending July 29); 4-week trend flat: balance sheet moved from approximately $6.72T (late June) to $6.75T (July 22)—change of ~+$0.03T (+0.45%), within the flat threshold; +0.4% YoY confirms no net QT acceleration; status supportive (flat to very slightly growing; no aggressive QT with rising overnight rates).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: VanEck mid-July 2026 Bitcoin ChainCheck reports perpetual funding rates at approximately +4.2% annualized 1-month average (equivalent to ~+0.004%/8h), down from +6.7% annualized (~+0.006%/8h) in late June/early July; CoinGlass returns HTTP 403 (proxy-blocked) this run; 30-day trend down: funding rates declined from ~+0.006%/8h in late June to ~+0.004%/8h currently, indicating moderating leveraged long exposure consistent with spot-led price action; status supportive (current rates well below the 0.04%/8h overheating threshold).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$303.2B as of July 12, 2026 (USDT $184.2B + USDC $73.4B lead at ~$258B combined); total crypto market $2.28T (July 27); dominance: $303.2B / $2.28T = 13.3%; updated from prior run's 13.4%; CoinGecko direct fetch 403; 30-day trend down: stablecoin supply contracted from ~$314.7B (June 21) to ~$303.2B (July 12) as capital rotated into risk assets; status supportive (30-day downtrend intact; headwind condition 'rising while TOTAL also rising' not met—TOTAL $2.28T flat while dominance declined).

upcoming.title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence / FOMC Meeting Day 1
upcoming.note: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index for July 2026 at 10:00 AM ET—1-year inflation expectations sub-component watched for anchoring signals as the FOMC convenes; two-day FOMC meeting begins July 28 (Tuesday); rate decision and Chair Warsh press conference on July 29 at 2:00 PM ET / 2:30 PM ET—non-SEP meeting (no dot plot); current target range: 3.5–3.75%; consensus strongly favors a hold; H.6 M2 release also July 28 under new IRA/Keogh methodology.

upcoming.title: FOMC Rate Decision & Press Conference (July 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve rate decision at 2:00 PM ET, Chair Warsh press conference at 2:30 PM ET—non-SEP meeting (no dot plot); current target range: 3.5–3.75%; consensus favors a hold; key watch: whether Warsh acknowledges back-to-back soft CPI and PPI prints as validating the disinflationary pipeline; a dovish hold could push DXY below 100 (currently 101.18) and compress real yields toward the 2.00% neutral threshold; next SEP meeting: September 15–16.

upcoming.title: Q2 GDP Advance Estimate / June PCE / BOE Rate Decision / Jobless Claims
upcoming.note: BEA Q2 2026 GDP Advance Estimate at 8:30 AM ET—first official read on Q2 economic growth; BEA Personal Income and Outlays (June PCE) at 8:30 AM ET—core PCE is the Fed's preferred inflation gauge; Initial Jobless Claims (week ended July 26) at 8:30 AM ET; Bank of England MPC decision at 12:00 BST—'Super Thursday' with full Monetary Policy Report and Governor's press conference; Bank Rate currently 3.75%; BOE voted 7-2 to hold at June meeting; WALCL H.4.1 release (week ending July 29) also due.

upcoming.title: BOJ Rate Decision / Employment Cost Index Q2 / UMich Final Sentiment (July 2026)
upcoming.note: Bank of Japan monetary policy statement released overnight ET (concluding July 30–31 BOJ meeting)—BOJ Policy Rate currently 0.75% (highest since 1995); BOJ will assess whether JPY dynamics and global disinflation justify further policy normalization; Employment Cost Index Q2 2026 at 8:30 AM ET (BLS)—the Fed's preferred quarterly labor cost measure; a hot ECI would complicate the post-FOMC dovish narrative; University of Michigan Final Consumer Sentiment (July 2026) at 10:00 AM ET—final 1-year and 5-year inflation expectations.

upcoming.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI (July 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM® Manufacturing PMI® Report for July 2026 at 10:00 AM ET—first major Q3 manufacturing activity read and first significant macro release after the July 28–29 FOMC decision; prior print: June 2026 at 53.3% (sixth consecutive expansion month); markets will watch whether expansion continues above 50, whether new orders (June: 56.0%) hold momentum, and whether prices paid (June: 73.0%) sustain the disinflationary signal; a fall toward or below 50% would reinforce late-cycle caution heading into the September 15–16 SEP FOMC.
